claims.text: The target material is defect-free HfNbTaTiZr with oxygen below 0.1 wt.%.
The proposed method combines DFT with phonon Boltzmann transport.
The proposed method computes atomic-scale phonon scattering rates caused by mass disorder.
The proposed method computes atomic-scale phonon scattering rates caused by force-constant disorder.
The proposed framework separates lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions.
Below 200 K, experiments on HfNbTaTiZr indicate comparable lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
From 300 to 1200 K, an oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr specimen has total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(m K).
Intrinsic mass differences and force-constant variability constitute important atomic-scale disorder in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicit ab initio force constants and alloy-scattering effects reduce the guesswork associated with simplified Debye or analytical methods.
Treating force-constant and mass disorder explicitly enables a more accurate prediction of lattice phonon conduction independent of electronic conduction.
The proposed method will predict lattice thermal conductivity within ±15% of experiment over 200–1200 K.
Prior approaches are expected to have prediction errors exceeding ±15%.
The proposed method is expected to improve predictive accuracy by approximately 25% relative to prior approaches.
Earlier methods neglect complex scattering from both force-constant disorder and mass disorder.
The model is valid only for specimens with oxygen below 0.1 wt.% and temperatures from 200 to 1200 K.
Higher oxygen levels introduce additional impurity scattering that can compromise prediction accuracy.
The estimated 25% improvement has an uncertainty of approximately ±10%.
Deviation of predicted lattice thermal conductivity from separated measurements by more than ±15% over most of the tested temperature range would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The motivating low-temperature observation is explicitly below 200 K, but the proposed validity range and falsification measurements begin at 200 K, so that observation cannot be tested directly within the stated applicability window.
